title: Ordinary shells a person opens and types into on this machine
description: The /v1/terminals routes (plan v3 §5). A terminal is an ordinary login shell on this daemon's own tmux server (internal/adapters/terminal/owned). Every local HTTP route needs this machine's own token or a paired device with send permission; typing, pasting, resizing and closing also need the terminal's one control lease. Clawdline Cloud terminal traffic uses the separate encrypted termi/term/termr wire in docs/cloud-terminal-wire.md; it does not turn a Cloud Router request into a local HTTP terminal request. Those requests still answer `terminal_cloud_not_supported`. Every refusal is a TerminalRefusal whose `error` is a TerminalRefusalCode.

TerminalStatus.description: Where a terminal is in its life. `exited` is a shell that ended on its own; `closed` is a terminal somebody closed, or one that is no longer there; `unreachable` is a server that did not answer, which is never a reason to call a terminal closed.

TerminalRefusalCode.description: Every refusal a terminal route answers with (plan v3 D4). A client branches on these and never on `detail`.

TerminalMouseMode.description: Which mouse reporting the program in the terminal asked for: DECSET 1000 (`standard`), 1002 (`button`) or 1003 (`any`).

TerminalCursorShape.description: DECSCUSR's shape as tmux names it. Absent from a cursor when the server does not say, which is drawn as `default`.

TerminalModes.description: The modes a program set that change what a key sends or what the screen is. A viewer puts its own terminal in the same modes before it draws a frame, so a key pressed there means what the program expects.

app_cursor.description: DECCKM: the arrow keys send `ESC O A` rather than `ESC [ A`.

TerminalFrame.description: One whole look at a terminal's visible screen: the `frame` event of the stream. A newer frame replaces an older one and nothing is ever applied on top of another, so a viewer that missed frames draws the newest and is right.

rev.description: A digest of everything but `at`: two frames with the same rev draw the same screen.

at.description: When the screen was read, Unix seconds with milliseconds.

rows.description: The screen's height. The text is `lines`.

lines.description: The visible screen, one entry per screen row, SGR escapes kept. A line longer than the terminal is as many rows as it wrapped onto.

TerminalHolder.description: Who holds a terminal's control lease, as the viewer being answered should read it. The holder's client id is never sent to anybody else.

name.description: The device's name: this machine's own, or the paired device's.

local.description: The holder is this machine's own token.

same_device.description: The holder is the device this answer is for.

same_client.description: The holder is the very client (browser tab) this answer is for: the `client` it sent, or named on the stream's `?client=`.

TerminalControl.description: A terminal's control lease: the answer to POST /v1/terminals/{id}/control and the stream's `control` event. One controller at a time; a lease lasts 30 seconds and is renewed every 10. Leases live in memory, so a daemon that restarts has none and the shells are still there.

epoch.description: The lease's number. Each acquire and takeover makes a larger one; an input names the epoch it was typed under and a sender numbers its inputs from 1 within it.

expires_at.description: When the lease lapses unless renewed, Unix seconds with milliseconds. Absent when nobody holds it.

applied_through.description: The highest input number typed under this epoch. Present only in an answer to the holder itself.

TerminalControlRequest.description: POST /v1/terminals/{id}/control. `client` is a random id the browser tab makes for itself; together with the device it names the holder. `acquire` while somebody else holds the lease is 409 `terminal_controlled` naming them; `takeover` ends their lease and they are told by a `control` event and `lease_superseded` on their next input.

dir.description: The directory the shell is in now.

TerminalList.description: GET /v1/terminals?project=. Every terminal on this machine's terminal server, narrowed to one project when `project` names one.

TerminalOpenRequest.description: POST /v1/terminals. The shell starts in the project's directory at this size. `terminals_full` past 8 open terminals on this machine.

project_id.description: A project id as /v1/work lists them.

TerminalInputRequest.description: POST /v1/terminals/{id}/input: raw keystrokes, base64, at most 4 KiB decoded. The holder numbers its inputs 1, 2, 3 … within an epoch and resends only with the same number: a number already typed answers `duplicate` and types nothing; a number past the next is 409 `input_gap` with `applied_through`. A tmux that did not answer leaves the lease's input state unknown, and every later input is 409 `input_state_unknown` until a new acquire.

TerminalPasteRequest.description: POST /v1/terminals/{id}/paste: text typed as one paste, bracketed when the program asked for bracketed paste. At most 1 MiB. Numbered from the same sequence as input.

TerminalInputResult.description: An input or paste that was typed, or had already been.

duplicate.description: This number had been typed already; nothing was typed now.

TerminalResizeRequest.description: POST /v1/terminals/{id}/resize. The holder only; the newest size asked for wins.

TerminalCloseRequest.description: DELETE /v1/terminals/{id}. The holder only: somebody who does not hold the lease takes it over first. Every viewer is told `state: closed` naming who closed it.

TerminalHistory.description: GET /v1/terminals/{id}/history?lines=N: up to N lines that scrolled off the top, then the visible screen. N is at most 2000; a larger ask is lowered.

TerminalState.description: The stream's `state` event. `closed_by` names who closed a closed terminal; absent for a shell that ended on its own (`exited`).

TerminalBeat.description: The stream's `beat` event, every 5 seconds: the viewer is still let in and the stream is alive. A viewer that hears no beat for longer than that treats the screen as possibly stale.

last_capture_at.description: When the newest frame sent was read. Absent before the first.

TerminalRefusal.description: Every refusal on a terminal route, and the stream's last `refusal` event before it ends (`terminal_access_revoked`).

detail.description: For a person reading a log; never parsed.

applied_through.description: With `input_gap`: resend from the number after this one.

TerminalGrantRequest.description: Legacy POST /v1/auth/devices/{id}/terminal. This machine's own token only, and never through Clawdline Cloud. The record remains readable for older clients, but terminal access now follows pairing and send permission; this grant does not change access.

granted_at.description: Unix seconds. Absent when not granted.

grants_ok.description: The legacy terminal grants file could be read. It no longer controls terminal access.

grants_error.description: Why the grants file could not be read.

streams.description: Terminal streams open now, of at most 16.
